title: Injection of toric boundary divisor classes into the complete local class group
statement:
Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and suppose it is sharp, meaning that $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $n\geq0$ be an integer. For a coefficient ring $L$, write $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ for the ring of finite sums of symbols $c z^q t^e$, with $q\in P$, $e\in\mathbf N^n$, $c\in L$, and multiplication $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. If $L$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$, let $B_L(P,n)$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q
eq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Let $R$ be one of the following rings: (i) $B_k(P,n)$ for a field $k$; (ii) $B_C(P,n)/(	heta)$ for a Cohen ring $C$ of residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $	heta-p\in(z^q\ (q
eq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. In case (ii), $p$ is prime and the residue field of $C$ is arbitrary of characteristic $p$. Write $z^q$ for the chart monomials in $R$. Assume that $R$ is a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and all $z^q$ are nonzero. Put $G=P^{m gp}$ and let $\sigma\subset G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ be the cone of nonnegative rational combinations of $P$. Let $\mathcal F$ be its finite set of codimension-one faces. For $F\in\mathcal F$ let $
u_F:G	o\mathbf Z$ be the primitive nonnegative facet form: its image is $\mathbf Z$, it is nonnegative on $P$, and $F=\sigma\cap\ker
u_F$. Put $\mathfrak p_F=(z^q:q\in P,\ q
otin F)R$. Assume these are distinct height-one primes and that the normalized valuation at $R_{\mathfrak p_F}$ takes $z^q$ to $
u_F(q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. A height-one prime is a nonzero prime with no prime strictly between it and $(0)$. Define $\operatorname{Div}(R)= igoplus_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q=1}\mathbf Z[\mathfrak q]$. For $b\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)^	imes$ write $\operatorname{div}_R(b)=\sum_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q=1}v_{\mathfrak q}(b)[\mathfrak q]$, where $v_{\mathfrak q}$ is the normalized additive valuation of the discrete valuation ring $R_{\mathfrak q}$; this sum has finite support. Let $\operatorname{Cl}(R)$ be $\operatorname{Div}(R)$ modulo the subgroup of all such principal divisors. Put
$$
u:G\longrightarrow\mathbf Z^{\mathcal F},\qquad g\longmapsto(
u_F(g))_F.$$
Assume the height-one primes meeting $\{z^q:q\in P\}$ are exactly the $\mathfrak p_F$. Then the homomorphism
$$ eta:\mathbf Z^{\mathcal F}/
u(G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cl}(R),\qquad [(m_F)_F]\longmapsto\left[\sum_Fm_F[\mathfrak p_F]ight]$$
is well defined and injective. In particular this asserts injectivity on all integer boundary-divisor classes, not surjectivity onto $\operatorname{Cl}(R)$. It includes $P=\{0\}$, when its domain is zero. Here $\operatorname{Cl}(R)$ is the Weil divisor class group, not the group of invertible fractional ideals modulo principal ideals.

source.place: Class-group input to the complete-local recognition equality: the cokernel of the primitive facet-valuation map injects into the Weil divisor class group of the completed model (the Mori-type injectivity issue in the return). ILO VI 1.4 and 1.6, printed pp. 69--70, motivate the model and the recognition problem; they do not state or prove this auxiliary theorem. Agent-formulated algebraic input for the direct divisor route. Kato (1994), Toric singularities, especially Theorem 11.6, is WANTED for the underlying toric divisor theory; no proof is attributed to an unread source.

proof.text:
For $g=a-b\in G$, with $a,b\in P$, the fraction $z^a/z^b$ has valuation $
u_F(g)$ at $\mathfrak p_F$ by the assumed valuation formula. At every other height-one prime neither monomial belongs to the prime, by the assumed exhaustive list of primes meeting monomials; hence both are units there and their values are zero. Thus $\operatorname{div}_R(z^a/z^b)=\sum_F
u_F(g)[\mathfrak p_F]$. Valuations add, so the map from the free boundary-divisor group is a homomorphism and annihilates $
u(G)$. This proves that $ eta$ is well defined. If $P=\{0\}$ its source is the zero group and injectivity is immediate; henceforth suppose $P
e\{0\}$.

source.place: ILO VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies the models only; the argument here is by Q29.

proof.text:
Use [lem-trf-sharp-cone-lattice-intersection] and the half-space formula of [lem-trf-complete-toric-facet-valuations]. They give that $G$ embeds in $V=G\otimes\mathbf Q$, that $\sigma$ is pointed, and that $P=\sigma\cap G=\{g\in G:
u_F(g)\ge0\  orall F\}$. If $
u(g)=0$, both $g\otimes1$ and its negative lie in $\sigma$, so pointedness gives $g=0$. Enumerate the $r=|\mathcal F|$ facets and set $M=
u(G)\subset\mathbf Z^r$; thus $
u(P)=M\cap\mathbf N^r$. Choose nonzero generators $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ of $P$ and put $c=\sum_jq_j$. For each facet some generator is outside it (otherwise the cone would be contained in that proper face); all facet values are nonnegative, so $w=
u(c)$ has every coordinate strictly positive.

source.place: ILO VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies the models only; the argument here is by Q29.

proof.text:
In either coefficient case put $B=B_L(P,n)$, $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_r,t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$, and $\widetilde M=M	imes\mathbf Z^n$. Its nonnegative intersection is $Q=
u(P)	imes\mathbf N^n$, generated by the images of the chosen generators and the parameter basis vectors. Renaming the polynomial basis by $z^qt^e\mapsto z^{(
u(q),e)}$ carries the completion ideal to $(\mathfrak m_L,z^v\ (v\in Q\setminus\{0\}))$; the inverse renaming induces inverse maps at every quotient, hence at their inverse limits. A field is complete at its zero ideal; a Cohen ring is complete at $(p)$ by [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Both have finitely generated maximal ideal. Therefore [lem-trf-completed-monoid-support-projection] identifies $B$ with the subring $A_Q$ of series supported in $Q$, by $z^q\mapsto X^{
u(q)}$, and supplies the $B$-linear retraction $ho:A	o B$ obtained by deleting coefficients outside $Q$.

source.place: ILO VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies the models only; the argument here is by Q29.

proof.text: In case (i) put $D=A$ and identify $R=B\subset D$; write $\bar\rho=\rho$. In case (ii) put $\Theta=\iota(\theta)$ and $D=A/(\Theta)$. Since $\Theta=\iota(\theta)$ lies in the supported subring, $\rho(\Theta a)=\theta\rho(a)$ for every $a\in A$. Consequently $B\cap\Theta A=\theta B$: if $b=\Theta a$ belongs to $B$, apply $\rho$; the other inclusion is immediate. Hence $R=B/(\theta)\to D$ is injective and $\bar\rho([a])=[\rho(a)]$ is a well-defined $R$-linear retraction fixing $1$. In both cases we may regard $R$ as a subring of $D$. For $v\in\mathbf N^r$, the projection formula gives $\bar\rho(X^v)=0$ when $v\notin M$, and $\bar\rho(X^{\nu(a)})=z^a$ for $a\in P$.

source.place: ILO VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies the models only; the argument here is by Q29.

proof.text: The common residue map is constant coefficient followed by $L\to k=L/\mathfrak m_L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring], $A$ is local and a series is a unit exactly when its residue is nonzero. If $b\in B$ has nonzero residue, its image is a unit in $A$, and $b\rho(b^{-1})=\rho(1)=1$, so it is a unit in $B$. A unit of $B$ has unit image in $A$, hence nonzero residue. Thus $B$ is local with this residue field. In case (ii), $\theta$ and $\Theta$ have zero residue, so their quotients $R$ and $D$ are local with the same residue field; an element of a quotient of a local ring by an ideal in its maximal ideal is a unit exactly when its residue is nonzero. The projection keeps the constant coefficient. Therefore if $v\in D^\times$, then $\bar\rho(v)\in R^\times$. This conclusion uses residue fields, not a claim that a module retraction preserves multiplication.

source.place: ILO VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies the models only; the argument here is by Q29.

proof.text: View $A$ as $B_L(\mathbf N^r,n)$: apply the supported-series identification [lem-trf-completed-monoid-support-projection] with the full lattice $\mathbf Z^{r+n}$, when every series is supported. In case (ii), the given condition on $\theta-p$ implies $\Theta-p\in(X_1,\ldots,X_r,t_1,\ldots,t_n)A$, since every nonzero chart exponent has a nonzero facet vector. Thus $D$ is one of the complete models for the sharp saturated free monoid $\mathbf N^r$. Apply [lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality] to obtain that $D$ is a normal domain, and then [lem-trf-complete-toric-facet-valuations] to this free monoid: its coordinate facets have boundary ideals $(X_i)$, which are distinct height-one primes, and every $X_i$ is nonzero. In particular the $X_i$ are prime nonunits in the domain $D$. These inputs concern a free-monoid model and do not invoke the recognition equality or the boundary-class injectivity being proved.

source.place: ILO VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, supplies the models only; the argument here is by Q29.

proof.text: Let an integer vector $(m_F)$ represent a class in $\ker\beta$. By the definition of the Weil class group choose $f\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)^\times$ with $\operatorname{div}_R(f)=\sum_Fm_F[\mathfrak p_F]$. Choose integers $N,H\ge0$ large enough that $m_F+N\nu_F(c)\ge0$ and $-m_F+H\nu_F(c)\ge0$ for all $F$, using the strictly positive vector from step 2. Put $b=Nc$, $d=Hc$, $h=fz^b$, and $h'=f^{-1}z^d$ in the fraction field. Their values are nonnegative at every boundary prime and zero at every other height-one prime. In a discrete valuation ring a fraction has nonnegative value exactly when it belongs to the ring (write it as a unit times an integer power of a uniformizer). Hence $h,h'$ belong to every height-one localization of $R$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), normalized valuation and uniformizer description; the valuation-clearing calculation uses the hypotheses of the item.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-serre-criterion-normal] to the Noetherian normal ring $R$ to obtain $(S_2)$. If normality is read as integral closedness of the domain, its prime localizations are also integrally closed: a common denominator $s$ outside the prime in a monic equation for $x$ makes the rescaled equation for $sx$ monic over $R$, hence $sx\in R$. Thus this is normality in exactly the cited criterion's sense. The domain $R$ is reduced, and $Q(R)=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. At height zero, the only prime is $(0)$, with localization this fraction field. At every height-one prime step 7 gives $h,h'\in R_{\mathfrak q}$, which means that a denominator outside $\mathfrak q$ clears each fraction to an element of $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-serre-s2-total-fraction-membership] separately to $h$ and $h'$; all its hypotheses now hold. It gives $h,h'\in R$, and their identity in the fraction field is the identity $hh'=z^{b+d}$ in $R$.

source.place: Tags 031S (lemma-criterion-normal) and 031T (lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1); apply the cited reduced-S2 membership statement twice.

proof.text: In $D$ the identity becomes $hh'=X^s$, where $s=\nu(b+d)\in\mathbf N^r$. Peel off its coordinate prime factors as follows. Induct on $\sum_i s_i$ for this product identity. For $s=0$, $hh'=1$, so $h$ is a unit. If $s_i>0$, the primality of $(X_i)$ from step 6 implies $h\in(X_i)$ or $h'\in(X_i)$. In the first case write $h=X_i h_1$ and cancel the nonzero $X_i$ in the domain to get $h_1h'=X^{s-e_i}$; in the second case write $h'=X_i h'_1$ and cancel to get $hh'_1=X^{s-e_i}$. Apply the induction to that shorter identity, adding $e_i$ to the exponent of $h$ only in the first case. The base case then gives a unit $v\in D^\times$ and $e\in\mathbf N^r$, with $e\le s$, for which $h=X^e v$. This is an induction using prime elements, with no factoriality assertion about $R$ or $D$.

As $e\in M\cap\mathbf N^r=
u(P)$, choose $a_0\in P$ with $
u(a_0)=e$. The identity in $D$ is now $h=z^{a_0}v$. Apply the $R$-linear retraction to obtain $h=z^{a_0}u$ in $R$, where $u= arho(v)\in R^	imes$ by step 5. Therefore in $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$,

u(a_0-b)\in
u(G)$, so its class in the source of $ eta$ is zero. This proves injectivity.

proof.text: The case $P=\{0\}$ was settled in step 1 without constructing a positive vector. When $n=0$ the lattice $\mathbf Z^n$, parameter variables, and parameter generators simply disappear in steps 3 and 6. The field and Cohen cases share the same projection argument; no perfection condition on the residue field, no surjectivity of $\beta$, and no recognition theorem are used.
